topicGaps: No separate official ophthalmic-pathology board exam or independent blueprint is listed in the cited current ABMS/ABPath sources; parent ophthalmology/pathology competencies remain an educational map, not a specialty examination blueprint.

Specimen accessioning, orientation, gross examination, sampling limits, report construction, and consultation workflow still lack long-form public video coverage; institutional supervised practice is not reproducible in self-study.
Anatomy, embryology, normal histology, and laboratory workflow have improved overview coverage but lack a coherent long-form integrated teaching sequence with specimen-to-report demonstrations.
Ocular-surface videos are more numerous, but scleral pathology, conjunctival lymphoid disease, infection-versus-degeneration distinctions, and tissue artifact interpretation remain unevenly covered.

Ancillary methods (special stains, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, molecular testing, assay controls, validation, and uncertainty) lack sufficient dedicated, observed long-form video instruction.

Rare orbital, optic-nerve, lacrimal and lymphoid lesions; pediatric intraocular differentials; metastases; and modern clinicopathologic classification need deeper case-based instruction than the public lecture set provides.
Image repositories and videos remain link-only unless the specific source grants a matching reuse license; case access is not permission to copy, rehost, or use in clinical diagnosis.
Six original teaching episodes are scripted but not clinician-reviewed, rendered, or uploaded; the residual 19.78 verified-hour gap remains real.
medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A requisition for a globe specimen lacks laterality and orientation. What is the best first educational workflow response?

options.text: Guess laterality from the referral diagnosis
Document the discrepancy and seek clarification before assuming orientation
Sign out a likely diagnosis from the photograph
Discard the specimen and request another

practiceQuestions.rationale: Accessioning and orientation are prerequisites to defensible gross/microscopic correlation. Never invent missing provenance; Hopkins describes gross examination, processing and clinical communication as program learning aims.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes the published Hopkins Ophthalmic Pathology Fellowship?

options.text: A three-year ACGME-accredited residency with a dedicated ABMS board
A one- or two-year fellowship with specimen processing, microscopic/molecular study, reporting and clinicopathologic correlation
A research-only non-physician postdoctoral position
A board-mandated examination course

practiceQuestions.rationale: The Wilmer page states one or two years and describes diagnostic/communication work; the directory labels the accrediting body Non-Standard. Neither source states separate board status.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which official source places ophthalmic pathology in ophthalmology residency education?

options.text: ACGME ophthalmology requirements specify pathology conferences and/or study sets across the disease spectrum
A standalone ABMS ophthalmic pathology subspecialty certificate
ABPath's ocular pathology subspecialty examination
A Johns Hopkins claim that this independent course is accredited

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ACGME requirements describe pathology education within ophthalmology residency. This does not make the separate Hopkins fellowship ACGME-accredited or establish a board.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner sees an abnormality on one de-identified whole-slide image. Which next step is most defensible?

options.text: Treat the image as sufficient to diagnose a real patient
Describe the morphology, review the case context and note what additional correlation is needed
Infer patient identity from metadata
Upload the slide to a personal public gallery

practiceQuestions.rationale: The MGH collection is explicitly de-identified and educational, but an isolated slide does not supply complete clinical context; its rights allow presentation use with attribution, not unrestricted rehosting.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which board-credential statement is supported by current official directories?

options.text: ABMS lists ophthalmic pathology as an ABO subspecialty
ABPath lists an ophthalmic pathology subspecialty exam
ABMS lists ABO ophthalmology with no subspecialties; ABPath's current listed subspecialties do not include eye pathology
A fellowship certificate guarantees ABO eligibility

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABMS directory states ABO Ophthalmology has no subspecialties, and ABPath's subspecialty list omits ophthalmic pathology. A separate fellowship completion does not establish ABO eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a morphology-first differential for a fictional eyelid lesion, which statement is sound?

options.text: One stain alone always uniquely identifies the lesion
Localize the lesion, describe its morphology and interpret any ancillary tests with controls and clinical context
Ignore tissue processing artifacts
A histology exercise authorizes a procedure

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pathology interpretation begins with tissue architecture/cytology and integrates appropriate ancillary results, controls and context; this self-study course does not confer procedural competence.

practiceQuestions.stem: A pediatric eye teaching case is described as leukocoria. Which approach is appropriate for an educational differential?

options.text: Assume retinoblastoma is proven by the sign alone
List a compartment/age-aware differential and distinguish the clinical presentation from tissue diagnosis
State a diagnosis and management plan for an actual patient
Use a repeated lecture to increase hours

practiceQuestions.rationale: Leukocoria has a differential; use the lecture to frame possibilities while requiring appropriate clinical/pathologic correlation. The fictional scenario is not a patient encounter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A digital educational slide repository says cases are de-identified and images may be used in presentations with acknowledgment. What is the rights-safe course practice?

options.text: Republish the whole slide set on a new public course site
Link to the source and, only if using an image in a permitted presentation, retain required attribution and conditions
Remove the watermark and credit nobody
Assume every other public image has identical terms

practiceQuestions.rationale: The MGH repository permits use in presentations with source acknowledgment; rights differ by resource, so do not assume one repository's permission extends to others.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which item is an appropriate learning outcome of a self-study course without human clinical review?

options.text: Board eligibility
Independent diagnostic sign-out privileges
Ability to describe a slide, formulate questions and identify uncertainty for supervised discussion
Competence to perform eye dissection

practiceQuestions.rationale: The online course can assess reasoning/description only; it cannot substitute for supervised clinical work, competency evaluation or credentials.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the correct interpretation of the phrase 'Non-Standard' on the Hopkins directory entry?

options.text: Proof of ACGME accreditation
The directory's listed accrediting-body status; do not relabel it as ACGME-accredited
An ABMS certification category
Proof that all applicants are board-eligible

practiceQuestions.rationale: The official listing explicitly says Accrediting Body: Non-Standard. Do not infer ACGME accreditation or board eligibility from the directory label.
